ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The applicant, all shareholders, all directors, all beneficial owners, all authorized signatories, and each vessel operator acting under the towage or salvage contract must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, the Korean autonomous sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Financial Action Task Force high-risk jurisdiction list. A licensed PEP database and an independent negative-media intelligence review must be run at engagement, refreshed before any Lloyds Standard Form wire is processed, and re-run quarterly. Any PEP link, high-risk jurisdiction, government-related source of wealth, or vessel flagged to a red-flag flag state triggers mandatory enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds evidence, source-of-wealth narrative, charterparty counterparty screening, insurance policy review, and board-level sign-off. All screening records, UBO attestations, and decision memoranda must be retained for at least five years after the close of the relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea, commercial registry name search and clearance module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be registered in Korean Hangul, with the mandatory statutory suffix Yuhan Hoesa for a limited liability company. Foreign-language or Romanized names must be rendered by official phonetic transliteration into Korean and may be supplemented by an English trade name only after the Korean statutory name has been registered. The Commercial Act requires a four-tier naming convention: a distinctive brand element, a descriptive business purpose element, a permissible territorial indicator, and the mandatory legal-form suffix. The English designation LLC or Limited Liability Company is not a valid substitute for the statutory Korean-name requirement and may appear only as a supplementary trade name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry official rejects the proposed name, the applicant must receive a written rejection stating the statutory ground. Within 14 days from receipt, a written objection must be filed with the same registry office, attaching revised articles of incorporation, a certified Korean translation or transliteration certificate, and evidence of distinctiveness such as a registered trademark, service mark, or brand-licensing agreement. If the official affirms the rejection, the applicant may commence an administrative suit against the relevant district court registry head under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days. An alternative name clearance may be submitted immediately; the rejected name may be reused only after the appeal is successful.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under Korean commercial-registration practice, the registered office must be a fixed and identifiable local address capable of receiving service of process, registered correspondence, and tax notices. A pure email-only or mail-forwarding virtual office is rejected by the Korean court registry for initial incorporation and by National Tax Service tax registration. For the maritime towage and salvage industry, the competent maritime authority and financial institutions will expect evidence of an operational place of business, including a lease contract, office signage, a local contact person, and a corporate bank account with transaction activity. A serviced office or office-sharing suite with a physical desk, postal handling, and a management service agreement may be accepted by the registry but is likely to be regarded by banks and the tax office as insufficient unless the company demonstrates actual personnel, records, and operating assets. Therefore, a physical office or a fully equipped serviced office in the jurisdiction is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspections by the National Tax Service, the relevant municipal taxation office, or the district court registration officer are possible during the first taxable year. Estimated quantified risk of a physical inspection within the first 12 months: 65%; within 36 months: 85%. Inspection checklist: original lease or ownership certificate; utility and management-fee invoices; physical signage; nominated representative present; office equipment and filing cabinets; board minutes; corporation books; VAT and payroll records; ship towage/salvage contract logs; crew appointment or subcontractor agreements; insurance policies; and a working computer with registered business email. Loss or surrender of the registered office before the first VAT return is treated as an indicator of shell status and may trigger de-registration and penalty.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (상법), as amended (Act No. 17905), Articles 287-1 through 287-31 on Limited Liability Companies (유한회사) and Article 289 (registration procedure), read in conjunction with Article 290; the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA), for non-resident shareholders; and the Registration of Corporation Rules, Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Division, Local District Court Registration Office (법인등기과) of the registered office seat; Seoul office: Seoul Central District Court Corporate Registry (서울중앙지방법원 등기과).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certified Articles of Incorporation (정관) and The Corporate Incorporation Registration Application (법인설립등기신청서) in the statutory form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under Korean Commercial Act for a 유한회사; capital is set in the articles and must be fully paid before registration. Foreign investment report may require inward remittance above KRW 100,000,000 but no statutory blocked escrow.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
The undersigned, constituting the Board of Directors of YUHAN HOESA (the Company), a company to be incorporated under the laws of the Republic of Korea, acting in accordance with the provisions of the Korean Commercial Act and the Companys Deed of Incorporation, hereby adopt, in person or by unanimity without a meeting, the following resolutions, effective upon the issuance of the corporate registration certificate.

FIRST: SUBSCRIPTION AND PAYMENT OF SHARE CAPITAL. The Directors resolve that the initial subscribed capital of the Company, as stated in the Deed of Incorporation, is allocated among the founding members according to the schedule attached herein; all subscription monies shall be deposited to the formation escrow account held at a bank licensed in Korea and shall not be withdrawn until the corporate registration certificate is issued. The Directors acknowledge that any foreign subscribers investment must comply with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, including the filing of an investment report and the use of a Korean-licensed foreign currency bank account.

SECOND: BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Directors authorize and direct the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer, acting on a dual-signature basis, to open and maintain corporate demand and settlement accounts at banks selected for the Companys operations, including an escrow account for the receipt of Lloyds Standard Form wire transfers, and to execute account authorization agreements, specimen signature cards, and electronic payment authorizations necessary to carry out the Companys marine towage and salvage business. The bank account signatories shall be subject to a joint approval threshold of KRW 100,000,000 and any amount above requires the additional approval of the Board.

THIRD: REGISTERED OFFICE. The Directors hereby adopt and approve as the registered office of the Company the address at [●], in the jurisdiction of [●] District Court, Korea. The CEO and Company Secretary are authorized to execute a lease agreement for such premises and to file the registered office address with the corporate registry and all relevant licensing and tax authorities.

FOURTH: APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Directors appoint [●] as Chief Executive Officer, [●] as Chief Financial Officer, and [●] as Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, each effective on the corporate registration date, with powers and duties as specified in the Deed of Incorporation. The CEO and the Company Secretary are jointly authorized to sign the corporate registration application and all other instruments in connection with the incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Office or Internet Registry System of the Supreme Court (인터넷등기소)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the corporate name 'Yuhan Hoesa' with the local court registry via the Internet Registry system (인터넷등기소) or at the District Court Registration Office. Draft the Korean-language Deed of Incorporation (정관) and include the scope of engaging in deep-sea tugboat towage, offshore salvage, and emergency marine rescue operations so that the business object covers ISIC 5222. Verify that the proposed name does not conflict with any licensed 'Hoesa' or trademark. After the draft is approved by all founding members, notarize the deed before an authorized notary public or a licensed attorney with notarial power. For any non-resident founder, execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. Prepare the deed in duplicate and keep copies for registration and bank escrow.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all founders and directors
Korean power of attorney for foreign founders
Notarized Deed of Incorporation (정관) in Korean
Name reservation confirmation from the court registry
Foreign Investment Report (if foreign subscriber)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, revise the trade name or add distinctive suffix and re-reserve. If notarization fails, correct the deed before a notary and request a supplementary certified page.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean licensed commercial bank and Korea Trade Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) for foreign investment declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary capital contribution escrow account at a Korean commercial bank in the name of the corporation, using the certified deed and founder identification documents. Instruct each subscriber to remit the subscription funds by wire transfer from their bank. The bank must issue a certificate of deposit (예금잔고증명) confirming that the paid-up capital has been credited and will remain frozen until the corporate registration certificate is issued. For non-resident subscribers, file an inward remittance report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and obtain the bank's declaration receipt. The certificate must bear the bank seal and be dated not more than seven days before the registration filing. Do not withdraw any funds until completion of registration.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening form and escrow agreement
Founder identification and proof of registration
Capital deposit certificate (예금잔고증명)
Inward remittance declaration receipt (for foreign funds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If deposit certificate defects, ask the bank to reissue the certificate with seal and date. If foreign remittance is refused, use the correspondent bank code and re-submit the foreign exchange report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Court Registration Filing and Issuance of Corporate Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Court Registration Office (법인등기국) of the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit to the District Court Registration Office a duly completed Corporate Incorporation Registration Application (법인설립등기신청서), accompanied by the notarized Deed of Incorporation, capital contribution certificate, consent forms of each director (and statutory auditor, if any), and proof of the registered office location. The court registrar will examine the legality of the object clause, the amount of subscribed capital, the qualifications of officers, and the legality of the registered office address. Pay the registration tax and education surtax via the court's designated deposit account. After review, the registrar issues a corporate registration certificate (법인등기증명서) showing the company's registration number and date. If the registrar issues a request for supplementation, correct and resubmit within 10 working days.
required_dossiers: Certified true copy of the Deed of Incorporation
Capital contribution certificate
Consent documents from each director and auditor
Proof of registered office (lease contract or consent letter)
Corporate Registration Application form
Receipt of registration tax payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court gives a correction order, submit the missing documents within 10 days. If application is rejected, examine grounds, amend filings, and file a new application or administrative appeal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution and Statutory Governance Implementation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and external legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board of directors meeting or execute a unanimous written resolution to approve the pro-forma first board resolution. In the meeting, formally adopt the registered office, appoint the statutory officers (CEO, CFO, Company Secretary, Head of Maritime Operations), and establish a dual-signature bank scheme. After the board resolution is signed, register the corporate seal (법인인감) at the court registry and open the company's main operating account at the designated bank. Prepare the beneficial ownership register under the Financial Transaction Reports Act and ensure that all officer data is filed with the corporate registry. Distribute the approved minutes to all members and record them in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: First board resolution original
Minutes and attendance register
Corporate seal registration application
Beneficial ownership register (if required)
Officers' appointment and consent forms
Bank signatory cards and authorization letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court refuses seal registration, obtain a notarized signature specimen. If BO filing fails, supplement natural person identification data and re-submit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Business Operation Licensing Alignment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Tax Office (관할세무서) and Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) Marine Transportation Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Post-registration, file a business registration application with the local tax office (관할세무서) to obtain the Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증). Submit a copy of the corporate registration certificate, the board resolution, the registered office lease, and the identification of the CEO. The tax office will assign a business registration number and issue documents for VAT and corporate income tax purposes. Notify the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries or the local Coast Guard that the company is operational, and file the application for the marine towage and salvage service license (per the industrial licensing section). Maintain all minutes, statutory records, and licenses on site ready for statutory inspection.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Application form
Corporate registration certificate copy
Board resolution for signing representatives
Rental agreement for the registered office
Application for marine towing/salvage license (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects the business registration, correct the owner data and re-file. If marine license is queried, provide operational safety certificates and financial solvency statements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF), Marine Transportation Bureau and Korea Coast Guard (KCG) Maritime Safety Inspection Unit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Marine Towing and Salvage Business Operating License under the Marine Transportation Act (해운법) and Offshore Salvage Operation Registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea (환경부) and Korea Coast Guard for coastal maritime waste and disturbance matters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category D - Exempt from mandatory prior Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) for offshore towage/salvage activities where vessel operation is temporary and no fixed infrastructure exceeds thresholds. Any shore-based residual facility must separately obtain an Environmental Registration (간이환경영향평가) or a Full EIA Report if occupied area exceeds 1,000 square meters in a coastal buffer zone.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: MARPOL Annex I oil content in processed oily bilge water not to exceed 15 parts per million; Annex VI sulfur content in marine fuel to be no higher than 0.50 percent m/m in Emission Control Areas from 1 January 2020; ballast water management per D-2 performance standard (less than 10 viable organisms per cubic meter in ≥50 µm size class); hazardous waste and residue handling under Wastes Control Act records and a licensed disposal manifest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Korean Register (KR) or authorized class society Fire Safety Certificate for hull structure and fire suppression systems; Korea Coast Guard Safety Equipment Examination and Civil Defense fire drill documentation; Ministry of Employment and Labor KOSHA Occupational Safety and Health Clearance for crew and shore support staff; ISPS Code Port Facility Security Clearance for tugs and salvage vessels.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea – HomeTax electronic portal (https://www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign non-resident entities must apply for a Business Registration Number (BRN) via the HomeTax portal or in person at the district tax office with jurisdiction over the entity's Korean place of business. Required documents include the certificate of incorporation, articles of association, proof of foreign registration, and a power of attorney if a tax representative is appointed. The NTS issues the BRN within 3-5 business days. For entities without a Korean place of business, a Foreign Entity TIN is obtained through the same process with a designated tax representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None (Korea does not have a check-the-box election; however, group taxation election under the Corporate Tax Act is available for domestic parent-subsidiary groups, and hybrid mismatch rules apply per OECD BEPS Action 2).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory for all business entities; no turnover threshold for corporations. For individuals, the threshold is KRW 10 million annual turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All B2B transactions must issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoice) through the HomeTax system within the prescribed reporting periods. Real-time clearance is not mandated, but e-invoices must be transmitted to the NTS within 1 day of issuance. Anti-fraud measures include digital stamping and validation via the NTS API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods are zero-rated under Article 21 of the VAT Act. For services, zero-rating applies to services supplied to non-residents for use outside Korea, including international maritime transport and salvage services. The service must be performed outside Korea or directly connected to exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: False zero-rating claims are subject to a 40% penalty on the unpaid VAT, plus interest. Retrospective clawbacks may extend up to 5 years. Criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment up to 3 years or fines up to KRW 30 million.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance, with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act administered through the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Inspection and the Korea Customs Service for declaration purposes
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a largely liberalized foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Korean won (KRW) freely convertible for most current account transactions and a broad range of capital account transactions subject to reporting, registration, or prior approval thresholds. Capital account liberalization is substantial but not absolute; foreign direct investment, portfolio investment, and borrowing transactions are generally permitted but require reporting to the Bank of Korea or designated foreign exchange banks, and certain transactions may trigger documentary verification including certificates of foreign currency deposit, tax clearance, and underlying contract evidence. For a Korean limited liability company engaged in offshore towage and salvage, the operational revenue stream will typically be denominated in US dollars or other foreign currencies, requiring the repatriation of export proceeds under the Foreign Trade Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The company must deposit received export proceeds in a foreign exchange bank account, and although there is no mandatory conversion of export proceeds into KRW, the exporter must report the receipt to the designated foreign exchange bank and comply with the receipt-within-18-months rule for export proceeds. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is allowed through a dividend remittance process that requires audited financial statements, corporate registration certificates, tax payment receipts, and a remittance application with the designated foreign exchange bank proving the source of funds and the tax withholding obligations under the Korea tax law. Stringent anti-money laundering verification, including ultimate beneficial owner disclosure and evidence of legitimate business operations, is applied to all cross-border fund flows, and the Bank of Korea maintains close monitoring of suspicious transactions. Practical hurdles for a newly formed entity include mandatory foreign exchange business registration, potentially lengthy bank KYC reviews for a marine services company, and the need to establish a clear paper trail for vessel ownership, charter contracts, and salvage awards before banks will permit outward or inward remittances. The overall convertibility regime is best classified as managed convertibility with high transparency but meaningful administrative friction for non-resident owners of maritime service entities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received in Korea within 18 months from the date of export declaration and deposited in a designated foreign exchange bank account; the exporter must submit a receipt report to the bank within 30 days of collection. There is no mandatory conversion ratio into KRW; the exporter may voluntarily convert export proceeds at the market rate, but any failure to receive the proceeds within the statutory timeline requires a pre-approval extension from the designated foreign exchange bank or the Bank of Korea.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for this entity because South Korea does not recognize unlicensed foreign fintech electronic money institutions as permissible banking counterparties for a domestic corporate entity; the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act requires cross-border payments and foreign currency accounts to be routed through a designated foreign exchange bank or a licensed financial institution registered with the Financial Services Commission and the Bank of Korea. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, or Mercury cannot provide a legal KRW account or act as a recognized settlement institution for the export of marine towing and salvage services unless they hold a Korean electronic financial transaction license, and even then the EMI would only be an intermediary and not a substitute for the required deposit bank. The corporate treasury must therefore rely on domestic tier-1 commercial banks for all KRW and USD settlement flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors and the ultimate beneficial owners must appear physically in-branch for the initial corporate account opening at a Korean tier-1 bank; remote consular proxy opening is generally not permitted for a newly formed Korean LLC. In exceptional cases, a qualified attorney-in-fact may attend with a notarized power of attorney, but every statutory director must still undergo an identity verification procedure, and at least one director with signatory authority must be physically present for the interview, with the bank also requiring a corporate seal certificate and real-office inspection for higher-risk maritime service entities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner is a non-resident with no Korean credit footprint and ownership in a maritime services company operating in international waters, creating jurisdiction-hopping and asset-invisibility concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the UBO's passport, proof of foreign residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months), structural chart showing the direct and indirect ownership of KR_YUHANGHOESA, beneficial ownership declaration obtained under the Act on Reporting and Using Certain Financial Transaction Information, sworn affidavit of source of funding for the initial capital injection, and a notarized explanation of the commercial purpose of the offshore towage and salvage operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank cannot verify the underlying vessels, towage contracts, and salvage awards referenced in the business plan, especially when the entity has no operating history or charter-party registry data
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid International Maritime Organization (IMO) vessel registration certificates or flag state registry extracts, classification society certificates, valid marine insurance policies (Hull and Machinery and Protection and Indemnity), signed towage and salvage contracts or framework agreements with the salvor or tugboat operator, correspondence with the Korean Coast Guard and Maritime Traffic Port Authority if applicable, and a certified income projection with corresponding charter rates and service invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: All directors are foreign nationals and none are tax residents of Korea, making it difficult for the bank to distinguish legitimate dividend distribution and profit remittance from disguised capital flight
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of each director's passport notarized by a Korean consulate, Korean tax registration certificates or a confirmation that corporate tax compliance is delegated to a certified tax agent and filing planned for all future periods, board resolution appointing a compliance officer within Korea, irrevocable appointment of a resident contact person with a valid alien registration card, and a written undertaking to respond to any Bank of Korea data call within five business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ISIC 5222 offshore towage and salvage scope may trigger enhanced screening for sanctions, terrorism financing, smuggling, and environmental crime because vessels navigate through sensitive maritime zones and jurisdictions with territorial disputes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Up-to-date Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), European Union, United Nations Security Council, and Korean Financial Action Task Force-compliant sanctions screening results for all counterparties, vessel IMO numbers, charterers, salvors, cargo owners, and final project sites; port call logs and voyage data records for the last 24 months or from date of incorporation; environmental compliance evidence (International Oil Pollution Prevention certificate, MARPOL compliance); and an internal AML/CFT procedure manual tailored to maritime client identification and geographic risk scoring.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from non-resident shareholders must be wired through SWIFT MT103 or MT202 to the company's capital escrow account at a designated Korean foreign exchange bank, using the Korean foreign exchange classification code for 'FDI: Korea Investment' or 'Investment in Domestic Company' as defined by the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. The remitter must provide the overseas bank with the company's Korean corporate registration number, the account number, the bank's SWIFT/BIC, and a clear purpose of payment such as 'CAPITAL INCREASE - INVESTMENT IN KR_YUHANGHOESA'. The receiving Korean bank will file the required FDI report with the Bank of Korea through the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) within 30 days of receipt, and the company must submit evidence of its business license, incorporation certificate, and foreign investor registration details to secure the capital verification certificate used for commercial registration and tax purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for towage and salvage operations, fuel procurement, port expenses, and subcontractor payments must be executed through the company's designated foreign exchange bank using SWIFT MT103 for direct cash payments, Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP 600 for large equipment and vessel charter settlements, and Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) for deferred payments to suppliers where bank-financed trade credit is not required. For any disbursement exceeding 50,000 USD or its KRW equivalent, the company must submit underlying documentation including invoices, contracts, customs declarations, and a written payment request confirming the transaction is not a disguised capital outflow.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: KRW/USD spot and forward contracts for trade receivables and payables up to 12 months tenor, with underlying export/import documents required

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW may be permitted for onshore companies through offshore banks only in limited non-trade financial transactions and are generally discouraged for trade hedging, so direct onshore forwards with Korean banks are preferred
Currency swaps are permissible only with the Bank of Korea's automatic approval system and are limited to term-matching of foreign currency debt and equity inflows, not speculative treasury positions

Margin and collateralization must be provided in the form of local currency deposits or government bonds, and the bank will require a board resolution and trade documentation evidencing genuine economic exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Base Computation Schedule for the prior fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of Korea; competent district tax office at the registered head office and the HomeTax electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than March 31 of the year immediately following a December 31 fiscal-year closing; if the deadline falls on a weekend or public holiday, the due date moves to the next business day; a limited extension of up to six months may be available for extra-territorial vessel operations only with advance approval of the competent regional tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing negligence surtax of 10% of the unpaid tax, rising to 20% if the return is not filed within six months; underreporting surtax of 20%, rising to 40% for intentional concealment; additional late-payment interest of 0.022% per day on the unpaid national tax until full payment; coercive collection by asset seizure and bank attachment may follow after 30 days from the payment demand; repeated non-filing can lead to revocation of the business registration by the National Tax Service, but not automatic judicial strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return for the prior fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Metropolitan or provincial government tax bureau where the registered head office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal-year end; for a December 31 fiscal year, by April 30 of the following year, to be filed simultaneously with the national corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing negligence surcharge of 20% of unpaid local corporate tax; non-filing surcharge of 40%; late-payment interest on local corporate tax at 0.022% per day; issuance of payment demand followed by compulsory collection and auction of vessel or tug assets after 30 days; no automatic administrative strike-off for delays, but continuous non-payment may cause revocation of the vessels' operating permits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy through the Foreign Investment Coordination Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal-year end; for a December 31 fiscal year, no later than June 30 of the following year; if any shareholder or member is a non-resident, the report must include audited financial statements and detailed ownership percentages
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to KRW 10 million for non-filing or false filing under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; cancellation of tax and tariff preferences granted to the foreign-invested enterprise; restrictions on dividend remittance and payments through bank escrow facilities until the report is restored; deliberate false statements are punishable by imprisonment up to three years and a fine up to KRW 30 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Audit Report and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic disclosure system; when a compulsory audit is triggered, the auditor report must also be attached to the corporate income tax return filed with the National Tax Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year, the audit report and audited financial statements are due within six months of fiscal-year end, i.e., no later than June 30 of the following year; the audited statements must also accompany the corporate income tax return due March 31 if the entity is size-tested as externally audit-subject
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or submit the report triggers administrative fines up to KRW 200 million and criminal fines under the Act on External Audit of Companies; the National Tax Service may reject the tax filing as incomplete, causing negligence surcharges of up to 20% and daily late-payment interest; directors and controlling members may become jointly liable for damages caused to third parties; the Financial Supervisory Service may also order an inspection and impose a corrective order, which in severe cases can lead to revocation of maritime transport licenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and Confirmation of Statutory Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Recorded in the statutory minute book and registers maintained at the registered head office; a certified extract is lodged with the court registry only where member resolutions amend the articles of association or change directors, statutory auditors or members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal-year end; for a December 31 fiscal year, the members' meeting must be convened by March 31 unless a court-approved extraordinary circumstance applies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing penalty is imposed because the obligation is internal governance, but each director is civilly liable to members and creditors for damages caused by delay or omission; continued failure to hold the annual meeting is a recognized ground for a court application seeking removal of directors or judicial dissolution of the company; without a valid annual meeting, dividend distributions are unlawful and can be reclaimed by creditors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Vessel Safety Certification Survey for each tugboat, salvage tug and auxiliary barge
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korean Register of Shipping or an authorized classification surveyor of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; enforcement through the Korean Coast Guard for port state inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual and periodic surveys must be completed on or before the anniversary date of each vessel's Safety Construction Certificate, Safety Equipment Certificate, International Load Line Certificate and Radio Certificate; SOLAS permits a survey window no earlier than three months before the anniversary date unless exceptional prior approval is granted by the classification society
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The vessel is detained until all safety certificates are restored; administrative penalties under the Ship Safety Act may reach KRW 50 million or imprisonment for up to three years; the vessel's registry entry may be suspended, P&I insurance coverage ceases, charter parties and Lloyds salvage contracts become voidable, and any incident arising from an un-surveyed vessel exposes the company and master to criminal prosecution and unlimited civil liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Marine Salvage and Towage Business Operation Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries through the Regional Office of Oceans and Fisheries and the Korean Coast Guard Maritime Traffic and Salvage Coordination Center
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than March 31 of each year for the preceding calendar-year activities, including number of towage and salvage contracts, assisted vessel tonnage, crew certification, insurance cover, and claims arising from offshore emergencies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to KRW 30 million for non-filing under the Marine Transportation Act and Ship Safety Act; failure to maintain the annual report status can lead to revocation or six-month suspension of the offshore towage and salvage business license; operational proceeds may be forfeited for unlicensed salvage acts, and the company may be excluded from participating in state-funded maritime emergency response tenders.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Companies, a mandatory independent audit by a Korean licensed CPA applies to a Yuhan Hoesa if any of the following quantitative triggers is met as of the immediately preceding fiscal-year end: (A) total assets are at least KRW 10 billion, approximately USD 7.6 million at the prevailing exchange rate; (B) from the 2021 phase-in for non-SME entities, total assets of KRW 5 billion or more; (C) annual gross revenue from towage, salvage, demurrage and ancillary maritime services is at least KRW 100 billion, with 300 or more full-time employees; (D) the Financial Services Commission designates the company as a public-interest corporation by reason of the size of the fleet, asset-backed securities issuance, or systemic importance in domestic coastal transport; (E) any bank, Lloyds underwriter, escrow provider, foreign buyer or project lender validly requires an audited financial statement under the relevant credit or salvage contract; (F) the National Tax Service expressly demands an external accountant certification due to suspected unreported turnover or application of a tax incentive for maritime salvage enterprises. When triggered, the audit must be performed by an independent Korean certified public accountant appointed by the members' meeting, and the resulting auditor report must be submitted to the Financial Supervisory Service and the National Tax Service.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards as adopted by the Korean Accounting Standards Board apply to listed and financial enterprises; a private Yuhan Hoesa engaged in offshore towage and salvage may alternatively apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles, including the SME Accounting Standards for small and medium enterprises. Revenue from long-term tug and salvage contracts is recognized under K-IFRS 1115 or the corresponding K-GAAP revenue standard, and tug vessels, life-saving equipment and floating assets are capitalized and depreciated in accordance with K-IFRS 1016 or K-GAAP Fixed Assets guidance. The accounting framework must be consistently applied and disclosed in the notes to the audited financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a publicly searchable annual UBO filing for a private Yuhan Hoesa; however, the company must maintain a members' register at the registered office as conclusive evidence of ownership, and any transfer of membership units must be recorded in that register within 30 days of the transfer. If the transferee is a non-resident, a foreign investment report must be submitted to KOTRA and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy within 30 days of the capital transaction. In addition, all share or quota transfers must be reported to the National Tax Service by the 10th day of the month following the transfer for gift and transfer-tax assessment. Financial institutions, escrow agents and Lloyds wire partners will require the company to confirm ultimate beneficial ownership at least annually as part of AML/KYC onboarding and before every payment rail instruction; failure to update the internal register or to notify the registered agent within the 30-day window subjects the directors and the registered agent to administrative fines under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and the Specific Financial Information Reporting Act.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 to USD 3,000 per year for registered office, registered agent, corporate seal custody, tax intermediary services, statutory register upkeep and annual general meeting administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 18,000 to USD 45,000 per year depending on fleet tonnage, number of open salvage contracts, bifurcated tug-and-barge structures, and whether IFRS or Korean GAAP is used

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million; 19% on taxable income over KRW 200 million up to KRW 20 billion; 21% over KRW 20 billion up to KRW 300 billion; 24% over KRW 300 billion, before the 10% local income tax surcharge (effective national-plus-local range: 9.9% to 26.4%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Yuhan Hoesa may benefit from: (a) Foreign Investment Promotion Act free-zone / national strategic industry tax holidays limited to qualifying foreign-invested enterprises with genuine Korean operations; (b) research and development tax credits for qualifying towage telemetry, autonomous-navigation, salvage-expert-system and marine-safety software; (c) job-creation and equipment-investment tax credits; (d) possible Korean Tonnage Tax election for qualifying Korean-flag international maritime cargo/passenger transport, but not normally for deep-sea salvage and dead-ship towage remuneration, which remains within the ordinary corporate income tax net. There is no general patent-box regime for salvage technology, but IP-derived income must be taxed at arm's length and qualifying patented R&D may generate R&D credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (법인세과세표준 및 세액신고서) and Local Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (hometax.go.kr) or an approved EDI service provider; the consolidated corporate income tax return package includes the Corporate Tax Base and Tax Calculation Statement, the Corporate Tax Return Summary, and the Schedule of Foreign-Invested Enterprise and International Transactions.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with semi-annual corporate tax prepayment obligations for continuing corporations; a non-resident corporation with Korean-source income but no domestic place of business files a separate annual non-resident return and pays via withholding.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within three months after the close of the taxable year; for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year. Where the deadline falls on a public holiday or Saturday/Sunday, it extends to the next business day. Prepayments are due within two months after the first six months of the fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Head-office identification, corporate legal name, Business Registration Number, corporate ID, fiscal year, principal place of business, number of foreign shareholders and foreign equity share, and status of non-resident directors/officers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Yuhan Hoesa must declare that Korea is its legal seat and central management and control location. If any shareholder or director is a non-resident, enter passport or foreign TIN, percentage shareholding, resident country, and a Korean taxpayer representative's address/telephone. Incomplete declaration is a red flag for hidden foreign ownership and may trigger banking AML enhanced due diligence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales and revenue from deep-sea tugboat towage, Lloyd's Open Form salvage awards, SCOPIC compensation, emergency-mobilisation fees, demurrage, incidental supply income and any foreign-source ocean-service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: As a Korean domestic corporation, Yuhan Hoesa is taxable on worldwide income. Long-term salvage and towage contracts must be recognised using the percentage-of-completion method in accordance with K-IFRS 1115; salvage awards must be accrued when the salvage service has been rendered and the award is virtually certain. Do not park offshore towage considerations in sub-accounts through foreign escrow agents; failure to recognise the full consideration is treated as fraudulent omission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and operating expenses: bunker fuel, tugboat depreciation and lease hire, crew wages and overtime, marine insurance, salvage equipment and ROV costs, towage subcontract fees, port and canal charges, pilotage, repairs, communications and foreign consultancy payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductibility requires actual performance, invoicing, contract documentation and bank settlement. Payments to foreign related parties must satisfy the arm's-length principle and must be separately analyzable in the transfer pricing exhibits; payments to non-resident subcontractors and agents are subject to 22% statutory withholding unless a treaty exemption or reduction applies. Fabricated invoices from shell suppliers will be disallowed and re-classified as dividends or taxable dispositions, not expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income: add-back of non-deductible expenses such as entertainment-over-limit, donations in excess of ceilings, corporate income tax, local income tax surcharge, fines, penalties, impairment of related-party receivables, and foreign-paid taxes not allowed; subtract tax-exempt income, dividends-received deduction, foreign-source income exemption, and prior-year tax losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The integrated return must attach the International Transactions Report and controlled-foreign-company computations if applicable. If a foreign affiliate is invoicing management fees that lack economic substance, those fees must be added back. Tax-loss carryforward is allowed for 15 years, but a change of 50% or more in ownership with discontinuation of the same business may reduce the loss deduction; non-resident shareholders restructuring their shareholding cannot preserve loss carryforwards without business continuity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computation and calculation of national corporate income tax using the progressive rates, application of the 10% local income tax surtax, alternative minimum tax and any tonnage-tax reconciliation for eligible international maritime shipping income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For Yuhan Hoesa the ordinary progressive CIT applies to salvage and dead-ship towage income unless the taxpayer validly elects tonnage tax for a separate qualifying international transport vessel. The local income tax surcharge must be computed at 10% of national CIT. If the entity is treated as a shell of a foreign beneficial owner, the National Tax Service may disregard the entity, tax the ultimate shareholder at a non-resident rate and impose secondary liability on directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits, prepaid taxes, and total net tax due: earlier provisional payments, wage and investment tax credits, R&D credits, foreign tax credits on foreign-source tug and salvage income, withholding tax credits from Korean payers, and net refund or payable for the fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders who receive distributions do not file on this corporate line; the Korean paying corporation must withhold at 22% statutory rate and remit the withholding to the tax office, or at a reduced treaty rate only after receipt of a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership declaration. The company must also issue dividend withholding statements and file the non-resident withholding schedule. Any foreign tax credit claimed for towage income taxed abroad must be supported by foreign return and payment evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the CIT return after the statutory deadline imposes negligence tax of 20% of the unpaid national tax (10% if filed within one month after the due date); underreporting or overstating expenses triggers negligence tax of 10% of the underpaid tax, which increases to 40% for fraudulent evasion. There is no daily 'late-return' surcharge, but unpaid tax accrues interest at the government lending rate and assets, including vessels and charter receivables, may be seized. Willful concealment of offshore towage revenue with intent to evade tax is a criminal offence under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, punishable by imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine of up to ten times the tax evaded, together with public disclosure of habitual evaders and travel restrictions during criminal investigation and collection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national corporate income tax withholding + 2% local income tax surcharge) on dividends paid by Yuhan Hoesa to non-resident corporate or individual shareholders, unless reduced by an applicable bilateral Double Tax Treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced DTA withholding on outbound dividends, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent authority of the residence jurisdiction for the calendar year of payment; (ii) complete and submit the Korean 'Application for Reduced Withholding Tax Rate under Tax Treaty' (and the related additional treaty-rate schedule) to the Korean paying entity, net financial institution, or the National Tax Service before payment or, at the latest, before the due date of the withholding return; (iii) prove 'beneficial ownership' with a written declaration supported by share register, financial statements, active business, and substance documentation in the residence state; (iv) disclose any conduit, back-to-back arrangement, or nominee chain; and (v) annually renew the application. If the statutory 22% was withheld, the shareholder may claim a refund through the non-resident return within the statutory statute of limitations, ordinarily three years from the end of the relevant fiscal year, by submitting the TRC, the withholding certificate, and full beneficial-ownership disclosure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-residents is statutorily subject to 22% withholding (20% national + 2% local surcharge), generally reduced to 0%-15% under most Korean DTAs depending on the identity of the payee and the nature of the instrument; royalty payments for towage software, telematics, salvage technology, or know-how are statutorily subject to 22% withholding and are commonly reduced to 10%-15% under DTAs, with some treaties reducing true 'user-paid royalties' to 5% under specified ownership conditions. Payments lacking economic substance, or excessive interest paid to a foreign shareholder that should be treated as equity, may be recharacterized as constructive dividends, rendering the payment non-deductible and subject to 22% dividend withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File: required when annual total revenue is at least KRW 100 billion and cross-border related-party transaction volume is at least KRW 10 billion; Local File: required when cross-border related-party transactions are at least KRW 10 billion; an Integrated Report of International Transactions is required when aggregate cross-border related-party transaction volume is at least KRW 5 billion. The National Tax Service may also demand contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation earlier during an audit whenever the transaction amount or pricing risk justifies it, especially for intercompany bunker, tug-charter, salvage-subcontract and management-fee flows.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: There is no UAE-style per-entity Economic Substance Regulation filing in Korea, but the combined effect of Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes (substance-over-form), the Korean controlled-foreign-company regime under the International Tax Adjustment Act, and the limitation-on-benefits/principal-purpose-test provisions of Korean tax treaties imposes a substantive Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) requirement. For Yuhan Hoesa, CIGA must be exercised in Korea: vessel ownership or long-term bareboat charter, vessel flag and registration, operational dispatch of tugs, crew employment and seamens' tax records, salvage risk management, commercial negotiation and invoicing, and financial accounting. If those functions are relocated to an offshore principal or a letterbox parent, the NTS can recharacterise the arrangement, disregard the interposed entity, deny treaty benefits, and attribute the income directly to the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Omission of Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to include deep-sea towage and Lloyds Open Form salvage award revenue in the corporate income tax return, including routing payments through foreign escrow accounts, issuing cash-settled invoices from Hong Kong/Tuvalu shell suppliers, making untraceable crew payments, and recording fictitious tug-repair or subcontract expenses to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 10 years and a fine up to ten times the tax evaded; Framework Act on National Taxes negligence tax of 10%-40% of underpaid tax and 20% late-filing penalty; automatic public disclosure of seriously non-compliant taxpayers by the National Tax Service; seizure of bank accounts, tug vessels, charter revenue, and port-use rights.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute or conceal a sham return are criminally liable as co-principals, not merely as corporate representatives. Korean courts will pierce the corporate veil where the Yuhan Hoesa is used as an instrumentality of the controlling foreign shareholder; directors and beneficial owners can be ordered to make full civil restitution of evaded tax, interest and penalties, may be blacklisted and subject to travel bans in Korea, and face imprisonment. The Commercial Act, Article 401, also exposes directors to third-party damages for gross neglect of duty.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Disguised Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging a foreign parent or affiliated shipowner above-market bareboat charter or salvage-subcontract rates; paying deductible 'management fees', 'mob-demob allowances', or 'terminal engineering royalties' to a no-substance offshore affiliate; buying tug-leasing services at excessive rates; failing to prepare Local File/Master File and the Integrated Report of International Transactions despite the relevant KRW 5 billion/10 billion thresholds; and distributing dividends as deductible payments to avoid 22% withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: International Tax Adjustment Act Articles 4 and 5 authorise the National Tax Service to make an arm's-length adjustment, compute the taxpayer's tax base as if the non-arm's-length transaction had not occurred, deny expense deductions, and recharacterise the payment as a dividend or capital contribution; the understated tax then attracts negligence tax up to 20% and interest; failure to submit documentation can lead to additional penalties and obstruction-based criminal referral; the scheme is reportable to the National Tax Service as a cross-border tax avoidance transaction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design or sign related-party pricing that lacks economic substance may be jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax deficiency under the substance-over-form doctrine and Commercial Act Article 401, especially where the arrangement is fraudulent or grossly negligent. Foreign principals who control the sham structure can also be personally named in the assessment; the NTS can impose travel bans during the audit/collection phase and criminal prosecutions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can result in imprisonment of the directors and beneficial owners.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Beneficial Ownership Concealment and Unlicensed Offshore Towage-Salvage Operations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominee shareholders, bearer beneficial interests, or undisclosed offshore trusts to own Yuhan Hoesa; failing to file Beneficial Ownership reports with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU); accepting Lloyd's wire, escrow, and high-value salvage awards without customer due diligence, source-of-funds verification, or suspicious-transaction reporting; operating deep-sea tugboat towage and maritime salvage without the required licence under the Marine Transportation Act and the Maritime Safety Act; and engaging in emergency salvage activity that causes uninsured marine pollution or oil-spill hazards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Articles 3 and 15), failure to report suspicious transactions or UBO information is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and fines of up to KRW 100 million; carrying on unlicensed towage/salvage under Korean maritime law can lead to criminal fines, administrative revocation of vessel registration, prohibition on port entry, and civil fines for pollution; the Marine Environment Management Act also imposes joint liability for oil-spill cleanup and environmental remediation costs.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced when the LLC is a façade for money laundering, unlicenced operations, or environmental harm; directors, managers, and beneficial owners may face confiscation of their personal assets, arrest and imprisonment, blacklisting of the individuals and the company, cancellation of the tug and salvage vessels' operating certificates, seizure of charter receivables, travel bans, and personal environmental clean-up liability under Korean maritime-pollution law. The signatories to the escrow and wire instructions can be prosecuted as accomplices for money laundering and financing of unlicensed maritime operations.
